title: Production Release Execution Safety, Environment Policy & Deployment Authority
productionSafetyGuarantees: Every production deployment executes through the existing authorization chain: authorization -> attempt -> project -> intent -> lease -> provider.

release.authorization.accepted / release.authorization.rejected are emitted at the authorization boundary with a specific reason (authorization_not_found, authorization_expired, authorization_revoked, authorization_binding_mismatch, authorization_replay).
provider.execution.blocked / provider.execution.permitted are emitted at the provider boundary; blocked paths never invoke the provider.

authorizeExecution retains Phase 138/171 invariants: durable authorization required, expiration enforced, revocation enforced, full identity binding (releaseId + artifactId + commitSha + environment), attempt-bound consumption (consumedByAttemptId must match the invoking attempt).

executeRelease retains Phase 171 durable attempt requirement: empty attemptId -> BLOCKED; nonexistent attempt -> BLOCKED; attempt whose job.payload.executionId differs from releaseId -> BLOCKED with zero provider calls.
Environment policy is explicit and code-defined: production/staging/development have deterministic requirement sets; unknown environments fail-closed to production policy.
environment-policy.ts introduces no new durable state; policy is deterministic (matching Phase 165-171 convention of code-policy + SQL-state).
Audit emission is best-effort: audit failures cannot change a decision; absent audit sink is a silent no-op, preserving pre-Phase-172 behavior.

Same-attempt retry does not burn an authorization (Phase 138 contract preserved); different-attempt reuse is blocked. Deployment-level idempotency remains enforced by the release-intent + bridge layer.
